audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 2 Kings / Melakhim Bet Ahaz, child-through-fire, Syro-Ephraimite siege, Assyrian appeal, Damascus altar, and temple alteration narrative, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for child sacrifice language, plural worship, siege, Elath population displacement, vassal language, sacred-treasury tribute, Damascus conquest and deportation, foreign altar copying, priestly compliance, temple reconfiguration, and imperial accommodation.

verses.restored: In seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham king of Judah became king.

familiar.text: In the seventeenth year of Pekah the son of Remaliah Ahaz the son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign.

modern.text: In the seventeenth year of Pekah son of Remaliah, Ahaz son of Jotham became king of Judah.

original.text: בִּשְׁנַת֙ שְׁבַֽע עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה לְפֶ֖קַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָ֑הוּ מָלַ֛ךְ אָחָ֥ז בֶּן יוֹתָ֖ם מֶ֥לֶךְ יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Twenty years old was Ahaz when he became king, and sixteen years he reigned in Jerusalem. He did not do what was right in eyes of YHWH his Divine, like David his father.

familiar.text: Twenty years old was Ahaz when he began to reign, and reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem, and did not that which was right in the sight of the LORD his God, like David his father.

modern.text: Ahaz was twenty years old when he became king, and he reigned in Jerusalem sixteen years. And unlike David his father, he did not do what was right in the eyes of the LORD his God.

original.text: בֶּן עֶשְׂרִ֤ים שָׁנָה֙ אָחָ֣ז בְּמָלְכ֔וֹ וְשֵׁשׁ עֶשְׂרֵ֣ה שָׁנָ֔ה מָלַ֖ךְ בִּירוּשָׁלִָ֑ם וְלֹא עָשָׂ֣ה הַיָּשָׁ֗ר בְּעֵינֵ֛י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָ֖יו כְּדָוִ֥ד אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: He walked in way of kings of Israel and even made his son pass through fire, according to abominations of nations whom YHWH dispossessed from before children of Israel.

familiar.text: But he walked in the way of the kings of Israel, yea, and made his son to pass through the fire, according to the abominations of the heathen, whom the LORD cast out from before the children of Israel.

modern.text: Instead, he walked in the ways of the kings of Israel and even sacrificed his son in the fire, according to the abominations of the nations that the LORD had driven out before the Israelites.

original.text: וַיֵּ֕לֶךְ בְּדֶ֖רֶךְ מַלְכֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וְגַ֤ם אֶת בְּנוֹ֙ הֶעֱבִ֣יר בָּאֵ֔שׁ כְּתֹֽעֲבוֹת֙ הַגּוֹיִ֔ם אֲשֶׁ֨ר הוֹרִ֤ישׁ יְהוָה֙ אֹתָ֔ם מִפְּנֵ֖י בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

verses.restored: He sacrificed and burned incense at high places, on hills, and under every green tree.

familiar.text: And he sacrificed and burnt incense in the high places, and on the hills, and under every green tree.

modern.text: And he sacrificed and burned incense on the high places, on the hills, and under every green tree.

original.text: וַיְזַבֵּ֧חַ וַיְקַטֵּ֛ר בַּבָּמ֖וֹת וְעַל הַגְּבָע֑וֹת וְתַ֖חַת כָּל עֵ֥ץ רַעֲנָֽן

verses.restored: Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel went up to Jerusalem for war. They besieged Ahaz but were unable to overcome him.

familiar.text: Then Rezin king of Syria and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to Jerusalem to war: and they besieged Ahaz, but could not overcome him.

modern.text: Then Rezin king of Aram and Pekah son of Remaliah king of Israel came up to wage war against Jerusalem. They besieged Ahaz but could not overcome him.

original.text: אָ֣ז יַעֲלֶ֣ה רְצִ֣ין מֶֽלֶךְ אֲ֠רָם וּפֶ֨קַח בֶּן רְמַלְיָ֧הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם לַמִּלְחָמָ֑ה וַיָּצֻ֨רוּ֙ עַל אָחָ֔ז וְלֹ֥א יָכְל֖וּ לְהִלָּחֵֽם

verses.restored: At that time Rezin king of Aram restored Elath to Aram and drove Judeans from Elath; Arameans/Edomites came to Elath and lived there to this day.

familiar.text: At that time Rezin king of Syria recovered Elath to Syria, and drave the Jews from Elath: and the Syrians came to Elath, and dwelt there unto this day.

modern.text: At that time Rezin king of Aram recovered Elath for Aram, drove out the men of Judah, and sent the Edomites into Elath, where they live to this day.

original.text: בָּעֵ֣ת הַהִ֗יא הֵ֠שִׁיב רְצִ֨ין מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֤ם אֶת אֵילַת֙ לַֽאֲרָ֔ם וַיְנַשֵּׁ֥ל אֶת הַיְהוּדִ֖ים מֵֽאֵיל֑וֹת וארמים בָּ֣אוּ אֵילַ֔ת וַיֵּ֣שְׁבוּ שָׁ֔ם עַ֖ד הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, Your servant and your son am I. Come up and save me from hand of king of Aram and hand of king of Israel, who rise against me.

familiar.text: So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglathpileser king of Assyria, saying, I am thy servant and thy son: come up, and save me out of the hand of the king of Syria, and out of the hand of the king of Israel, which rise up against me.

modern.text: So Ahaz sent messengers to Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria, saying, “I am your servant and your son. Come up and save me from the hands of the kings of Aram and Israel, who are rising up against me.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח אָחָ֜ז מַלְאָכִ֗ים אֶל תִּ֠גְלַת פְּלֶ֤סֶר מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר עַבְדְּךָ֥ וּבִנְךָ֖ אָ֑נִי עֲלֵ֨ה וְהוֹשִׁעֵ֜נִי מִכַּ֣ף מֶֽלֶךְ אֲרָ֗ם וּמִכַּף֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הַקּוֹמִ֖ים עָלָֽי

verses.restored: Ahaz took silver and gold found in house of YHWH and treasuries of king's house and sent a gift to king of Assyria.

familiar.text: And Ahaz took the silver and gold that was found in the house of the LORD, and in the treasures of the king’s house, and sent it for a present to the king of Assyria.

modern.text: Ahaz also took the silver and gold found in the house of the LORD and in the treasuries of the king’s palace, and he sent it as a gift to the king of Assyria.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֨ח אָחָ֜ז אֶת הַכֶּ֣סֶף וְאֶת הַזָּהָ֗ב הַנִּמְצָא֙ בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֔ה וּבְאֹֽצְר֖וֹת בֵּ֣ית הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁלַ֥ח לְמֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁ֖וּר שֹֽׁחַד

verses.restored: King of Assyria listened to him. King of Assyria went up against Damascus, captured it, exiled its people to Kir, and put Rezin to death.

familiar.text: And the king of Assyria hearkened unto him: for the king of Assyria went up against Damascus, and took it, and carried the people of it captive to Kir, and slew Rezin.

modern.text: So the king of Assyria responded to him, marched up to Damascus, and captured it. He took its people to Kir as captives and put Rezin to death. The Idolatry of Ahaz (2 Chronicles 28:16–27)

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֵלָיו֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ אַשּׁ֔וּר וַיַּעַל֩ מֶ֨לֶךְ אַשּׁ֤וּר אֶל דַּמֶּ֨שֶׂק֙ וַֽיִּתְפְּשֶׂ֔הָ וַיַּגְלֶ֖הָ קִ֑ירָה וְאֶת רְצִ֖ין הֵמִֽית

verses.restored: King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria and saw altar in Damascus. King Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest likeness of altar and its pattern according to all its workmanship.

familiar.text: And king Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglathpileser king of Assyria, and saw an altar that was at Damascus: and king Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest the fashion of the altar, and the pattern of it, according to all the workmanship thereof.

modern.text: Then King Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-pileser king of Assyria. On seeing the altar in Damascus, King Ahaz sent Uriah the priest a model of the altar and complete plans for its construction.

original.text: וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ אָחָ֡ז לִ֠קְרַאת תִּגְלַ֨ת פִּלְאֶ֤סֶר מֶֽלֶךְ אַשּׁוּר֙ דּוּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וַיַּ֥רְא אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּדַמָּ֑שֶׂק וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז אֶל אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֗ן אֶת דְּמ֧וּת הַמִּזְבֵּ֛חַ וְאֶת תַּבְנִית֖וֹ לְכָֽל מַעֲשֵֽׂהוּ

verses.restored: Urijah the priest built altar according to all king Ahaz sent from Damascus; thus Urijah the priest made it before king Ahaz returned from Damascus.

familiar.text: And Urijah the priest built an altar according to all that king Ahaz had sent from Damascus: so Urijah the priest made it against king Ahaz came from Damascus.

modern.text: And Uriah the priest built the altar according to all the instructions King Ahaz had sent from Damascus, and he completed it by the time King Ahaz had returned.

original.text: וַיִּ֛בֶן אוּרִיָּ֥ה הַכֹּהֵ֖ן אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ כְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר שָׁלַח֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז מִדַּמֶּ֗שֶׂק כֵּ֤ן עָשָׂה֙ אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֔ן עַד בּ֥וֹא הַמֶּֽלֶךְ אָחָ֖ז מִדַּמָּֽשֶׂק

verses.restored: King came from Damascus, saw altar, approached altar, and offered upon it.

familiar.text: And when the king was come from Damascus, the king saw the altar: and the king approached to the altar, and offered thereon.

modern.text: When the king came back from Damascus and saw the altar, he approached it and presented offerings on it.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֤א הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ מִדַּמֶּ֔שֶׂק וַיַּ֥רְא הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אֶת הַמִּזְבֵּ֑חַ וַיִּקְרַ֥ב הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ וַיַּ֥עַל עָלָֽיו

verses.restored: He sent up his burnt offering and grain offering, poured his drink offering, and dashed blood of his peace offerings upon altar.

familiar.text: And he burnt his burnt offering and his meat offering, and poured his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings, upon the altar.

modern.text: He offered his burnt offering and his grain offering, poured out his drink offering, and sprinkled the blood of his peace offerings on the altar.

original.text: וַיַּקְטֵ֤ר אֶת עֹֽלָתוֹ֙ וְאֶת מִנְחָת֔וֹ וַיַּסֵּ֖ךְ אֶת נִסְכּ֑וֹ וַיִּזְרֹ֛ק אֶת דַּֽם הַשְּׁלָמִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר ל֖וֹ עַל הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ

verses.restored: Bronze altar that was before YHWH he brought from front of house, from between new altar and house of YHWH, and placed it on north side of new altar.

familiar.text: And he brought also the brasen altar, which was before the LORD, from the forefront of the house, from between the altar and the house of the LORD, and put it on the north side of the altar.

modern.text: He also took the bronze altar that stood before the LORD from the front of the temple (between the new altar and the house of the LORD) and he put it on the north side of the new altar.

original.text: וְאֵ֨ת הַמִּזְבַּ֣ח הַנְּחֹשֶׁת֮ אֲשֶׁ֣ר לִפְנֵ֣י יְהוָה֒ וַיַּקְרֵ֗ב מֵאֵת֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַבַּ֔יִת מִבֵּין֙ הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וּמִבֵּ֖ין בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּתֵּ֥ן אֹת֛וֹ עַל יֶ֥רֶךְ הַמִּזְבֵּ֖חַ צָפֽוֹנָה

verses.restored: King Ahaz commanded Urijah the priest, saying, Upon great altar send up morning burnt offering, evening grain offering, king's burnt offering and grain offering, burnt offering of all people of land, their grain offering and drink offerings; all blood of burnt offering and sacrifice you shall dash upon it. Bronze altar shall be for me to inquire/consider.

familiar.text: And king Ahaz commanded Urijah the priest, saying, Upon the great altar burn the morning burnt offering, and the evening meat offering, and the king’s burnt sacrifice, and his meat offering, with the burnt offering of all the people of the land, and their meat offering, and their drink offerings; and sprinkle upon it all the blood of the burnt offering, and all the blood of the sacrifice: and the brasen altar shall be for me to enquire by.

modern.text: Then King Ahaz commanded Uriah the priest, “Offer on the great altar the morning burnt offering, the evening grain offering, and the king’s burnt offering and grain offering, as well as the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings of all the people of the land. Sprinkle on the altar all the blood of the burnt offerings and sacrifices. But I will use the bronze altar to seek guidance.”

original.text: ויצוהו הַמֶּֽלֶךְ אָ֠חָז אֶת אוּרִיָּ֨ה הַכֹּהֵ֜ן לֵאמֹ֗ר עַ֣ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֣חַ הַגָּד֡וֹל הַקְטֵ֣ר אֶת עֹֽלַת הַבֹּקֶר֩ וְאֶת מִנְחַ֨ת הָעֶ֜רֶב וְֽאֶת עֹלַ֧ת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ וְאֶת מִנְחָת֗וֹ וְ֠אֵת עֹלַ֞ת כָּל עַ֤ם הָאָ֨רֶץ֙ וּמִנְחָתָ֣ם וְנִסְכֵּיהֶ֔ם וְכָל דַּ֥ם עֹלָ֛ה וְכָל דַּם זֶ֖בַח עָלָ֣יו תִּזְרֹ֑ק וּמִזְבַּ֧ח הַנְּחֹ֛שֶׁת יִֽהְיֶה לִּ֖י לְבַקֵּֽר

verses.restored: Urijah the priest did according to all king Ahaz commanded.

familiar.text: Thus did Urijah the priest, according to all that king Ahaz commanded.

modern.text: So Uriah the priest did just as King Ahaz had commanded.

original.text: וַיַּ֖עַשׂ אוּרִיָּ֣ה הַכֹּהֵ֑ן כְּכֹ֥ל אֲשֶׁר צִוָּ֖ה הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אָחָֽז

verses.restored: King Ahaz cut off panels of stands and removed basins from upon them; he took sea down from bronze cattle beneath it and placed it upon pavement of stones.

familiar.text: And king Ahaz cut off the borders of the bases, and removed the laver from off them; and took down the sea from off the brasen oxen that were under it, and put it upon a pavement of stones.

modern.text: King Ahaz also cut off the frames of the movable stands and removed the bronze basin from each of them. He took down the Sea from the bronze oxen that were under it and put it on a stone base.

original.text: וַיְקַצֵּץ֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ אָחָ֜ז אֶת הַמִּסְגְּר֣וֹת הַמְּכֹנ֗וֹת וַיָּ֤סַר מֵֽעֲלֵיהֶם֙ ואת הַכִּיֹּ֔ר וְאֶת הַיָּ֣ם הוֹרִ֔ד מֵעַ֛ל הַבָּקָ֥ר הַנְּחֹ֖שֶׁת אֲשֶׁ֣ר תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ וַיִּתֵּ֣ן אֹת֔וֹ עַ֖ל מַרְצֶ֥פֶת אֲבָנִֽים

verses.restored: Covered Sabbath structure they built in house and outer entrance of king he turned from house of YHWH because of king of Assyria.

familiar.text: And the covert for the sabbath that they had built in the house, and the king’s entry without, turned he from the house of the LORD for the king of Assyria.

modern.text: And on account of the king of Assyria, he removed the Sabbath canopy they had built in the temple and closed the royal entryway outside the house of the LORD.

original.text: וְאֶת מיסך הַשַּׁבָּ֜ת אֲשֶׁר בָּנ֣וּ בַבַּ֗יִת וְאֶת מְב֤וֹא הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ הַֽחִיצ֔וֹנָה הֵסֵ֖ב בֵּ֣ית יְהוָ֑ה מִפְּנֵ֖י מֶ֥לֶךְ אַשּֽׁוּר

verses.restored: Remaining acts of Ahaz that he did, are they not written in scroll of matters of days of kings of Judah?

familiar.text: Now the rest of the acts of Ahaz which he did, are they not written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Judah?

modern.text: As for the rest of the acts of Ahaz, along with his accomplishments, are they not written in the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Judah?

original.text: וְיֶ֛תֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י אָחָ֖ז אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָׂ֑ה הֲלֹא הֵ֣ם כְּתוּבִ֗ים עַל סֵ֛פֶר דִּבְרֵ֥י הַיָּמִ֖ים לְמַלְכֵ֥י יְהוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Ahaz lay with his fathers and was buried with his fathers in city of David. Hezekiah his son became king in his place.

familiar.text: And Ahaz slept with his fathers, and was buried with his fathers in the city of David: and Hezekiah his son reigned in his stead.

modern.text: And Ahaz rested with his fathers and was buried with them in the City of David, and his son Hezekiah reigned in his place.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁכַּ֤ב אָחָז֙ עִם אֲבֹתָ֔יו וַיִּקָּבֵ֥ר עִם אֲבֹתָ֖יו בְּעִ֣יר דָּוִ֑ד וַיִּמְלֹ֛ךְ חִזְקִיָּ֥הוּ בְנ֖וֹ תַּחְתָּֽיו

translation_notes: Making a child 'pass through fire' is child endangerment or sacrifice and must be treated as abuse, not spiritual devotion, parental right, or cultural curiosity.
The nations named in polemical comparison must not become targets of ethnic contempt. Ahaz remains responsible for his own choices.
The siege by Aram and Israel threatens Jerusalem, while Elath's population is displaced and replaced. Territorial changes contain human removal, not only royal maps.

Ahaz calls himself Assyria's servant and son and pays with temple and palace treasure. The alliance relieves one threat by deepening imperial dependence and enabling Damascus's conquest and deportation.
Damascus's people are exiled to Kir and Rezin is executed. Judah's rescue is purchased through another population's suffering.
Copying a foreign altar is not inherently wrong because it is foreign; the ethical questions concern royal power, coercion, resource use, and the redirection of public worship.
Urijah complies with royal instructions before Ahaz returns. Priestly obedience to a ruler is not automatically faithfulness and does not erase institutional responsibility.

Temple objects are altered for imperial accommodation. Sacred traditions can be reorganized under political pressure, and no later reader should turn this into hostility toward artistic or interfaith exchange.
Chronology, the Elath reading, and the function of the bronze altar require textual and historical audit.
safety_note: Do not normalize child sacrifice, demonize foreign peoples or religious art, excuse priestly compliance with coercive power, or treat Assyrian intervention as clean rescue. Center the child, displaced Elath residents, deported Damascenes, and the way frightened rulers can trade communal treasure and institutional independence for imperial protection.
